# Multi-Granularity Hybrid Retrieval {#sec-retrieval}

A query is an `Ephemeral` signal of any modality. It is embedded like any
other signal, runs inside a transaction that is rolled back, and leaves no
trace in the store. This section specifies how its candidate pool is built,
fused and reranked. @sec-hydration specifies what is attached to the selected
memories afterwards.

Ingest-time retrieval, which feeds the streaming interrupt gate
(@sec-interrupt), uses only the dense unit channel. Lexical seeds were
measured at ingest too: they cost per-turn time without improving recall.

## Notation

* $q$: the query, with unit embedding $e_q \in \mathbb{R}^{256}$, modality
  $\mu_q$, text payload (if any), and optional reference time $T_q$ with flag
  `as_of`.
* $\mathcal{M}$: the long-term memories. Memory $m$ has a pooled
  representative $e_m$ (@sec-rep-embedding), a time span
  $[\mathrm{start}_m, \mathrm{end}_m]$, and member signals $s \in m$.
* Member $s$ has a stored shared-space vector $v_s$ (`memory_signal_vectors`,
  migration 50, keyed by the payload's content id) and a late-interaction
  code set $Z_s$ (`memory_signal_li_codes`, migration 54).
* $\tau_x$: the exclusion time. It is the start of the query's still-open
  write unit, so a query never retrieves itself. With `as_of` set,
  $\tau_x \leftarrow \min(\tau_x, T_q + 1)$ on every channel.
* $\operatorname{map01}(c) = (c + 1)/2$.

A memory is *seed-eligible* when it is `LONG_TERM`, has a vector surface and
started before $\tau_x$. Every channel resolves its hits through the same
eligibility test.

## Dense Unit Seeds

The base channel ranks memories by
$\operatorname{map01}(\cos(e_q, e_m))$ over the current long-term surface.
Above a knob-derived population, candidates come from the sparse route, and
the exact SQL path runs whenever the route cannot certify a full seed set
(@sec-optimization).

Before the seed cap, near-duplicate embedding families collapse to one
representative. The sound block-norm screens of @sec-optimization keep this
from costing quadratic work. Superseded memories stay eligible: excluding
them was measured as harmful (@sec-negative).

The seed count is $\operatorname{round}(\operatorname{lerp}(96, 8, f))$, where
$f$ is the retrieval Focus bias, and the seed search breadth expands it
further. At neutral knobs the engine seeds 37 memories from a search breadth
of 345 and returns 11.

## Member Seeds

A unit grouped from several signals has one pooled vector. That vector sits
between its members and is close to none of them. A query about one member
therefore ranks the unit far below where that member alone would rank. The
member channel scores each multi-signal memory by its best member:

$$
\mathrm{seed}(m) = \max\Big(\operatorname{map01}(\cos(e_q, e_m)),\;
                       \max_{s \in m} \operatorname{map01}(\cos(e_q, v_s))\Big).
$$

The 20 memories with the best members join the seed set, or raise the seed
score of a memory already in it. The seed list is then re-sorted. Member
vectors stay resident as int8 codes with one scale per vector
(dimension + 4 bytes per member). Single-signal memories are never held,
because their member vector is their memory vector. Each hit is resolved to
its current memory through the store before use.

Member scoring was measured as the third of three stages against the
Natural baseline. The first was query focus, which keeps a grouped memory's
query-nearest members and was the precursor of evidence fitting
(@sec-hydration). The second was the per-signal standing set. On BEAM, the
three stages together raised the gold-turn share of the 8,000-token packet
from 0.385 / 0.195 / 0.125 to 0.617 / 0.420 / 0.272 at 100K / 1M / 10M. The
past.dev-protocol score, answered and judged by gpt-5.6-luna, rose from
0.793 / 0.750 / 0.651 to 0.847 / 0.813 / 0.718 (+0.054 [0.019, 0.095],
+0.062 [0.044, 0.081], +0.067 [0.029, 0.100]). Measured on its own, member scoring
moved the score by +0.018 [+0.002, +0.034] at 100K and +0.013 [−0.003, +0.032]
at 1M, and raised 1M gold share by +0.036 [+0.022, +0.050] (hill-climb
record; @sec-implementation).

## Keyword Seeds: FTS5 BM25

Every stored long-term text memory is indexed in a contentless SQLite FTS5
table, `memory_text_fts` (migration 49). Its rowid is the memory id, its tokens
are porter-stemmed `unicode61`, and the text itself stays in the object store.
The index row is written in the savepoint that writes the memory, so it
commits, rolls back and is deleted with it.

A text query ORs at most 16 of its non-stopword words, each as a quoted FTS5
string. It drops any word whose index term occurs in more than
$\max(64, 0.05N)$ of the $N$ memories. Such terms carry little BM25 weight,
and their posting lists dominated query time. The 20 best eligible hits by
`bm25()` [@robertson2009probabilistic] form the keyword list, collected
without sorting every match (@sec-optimization).

The channel targets turns that share a query's rare words (names, numbers)
but sit far down the vector ranking. The shipped channel (FTS5 with the
document-frequency cut, commit ec30c69f) was measured against the pruned
vector-only engine (47c18ec9), with Haiku judging (rubric v2):

* Eval 1, 250 cases: packet gold-turn recall rose from 0.597 to 0.787 (70
  cases better, 6 worse). Judged sufficiency rose by +0.132 ± 0.065 (train)
  and +0.222 ± 0.060 (test).
* LongMemEval-M, 48 haystacks of about 4.9k turns: packet recall rose from
  0.407 to 0.667, and judged sufficiency from 0.530 to 0.821
  (+0.292 ± 0.112). Query p95 and ingest time stayed within 2%.

PR #28 reports the larger v2-against-47c18ec9 comparison (Eval 1 recall
0.597 → 0.809, sufficiency +0.149 ± 0.063 / +0.218 ± 0.059). That
comparison includes the other v2 changes as well as the keyword channel.

## Cross-Modal Seeds

AIST maps text, audio and images into one space, but cosines across
modalities sit far below cosines within one. A matching image scores about as
high as unrelated text. Raw cosine would therefore never let an image answer
a text query. The cross-modal channel ranks each stored modality $\mu \ne
\mu_q$ in its own list and gap-corrects it with a per-query z-score over that
modality's whole long-term population $P_\mu$ of signal vectors:

$$
z_s = \big(\cos(e_q, v_s) - \bar{c}_\mu\big) / \sigma_\mu,
$$

where $\bar{c}_\mu$ and $\sigma_\mu$ are the mean and standard deviation of
$\cos(e_q, v_s)$ over $s \in P_\mu$. A memory takes its best member's $z$. It is kept when $z \ge 1.5$ and
$|P_\mu| \ge 3$, and each modality contributes at most 3 memories. Same-modality
recall stays with the dense channel. Populations stay resident per modality
and advance incrementally (@sec-optimization).

This channel shipped with the other multimodal changes: per-stream signal
filtering, mixed-modality memories that keep every payload, and a vectorized
image tower. Together they raised MemLens image-evidence recall from 0.558 to
0.744 against an oracle ceiling of 0.867, and lowered the misleading rate from
0.028 to 0.009, with text packets unchanged (PR #28).

## Temporal Seeds

A query may carry a reference time $T_q$, in the past or the future
(`Cortext::RetrievalTime`). The engine treats it as signal metadata compared
with stored times, never as text, so it works the same for every modality.
The temporal channel returns the $K = 10$ eligible memories nearest $T_q$ by
interval distance:

$$
d(m, T_q) = \max\big(0,\; \mathrm{start}_m - T_q,\; T_q - \mathrm{end}_m\big),
$$

which is 0 when $T_q$ falls inside $[\mathrm{start}_m, \mathrm{end}_m]$ and
otherwise the distance to the nearer edge.

One statement with three range scans, over partial indexes on long-term
`start_ts` and `end_ts` (migration 55), each limited to $2K + 4$ rows, finds
them in $O(\log N + K)$. A test asserts the query plan has no `SCAN
memories`. The channel only adds candidates and rank mass, with weight 0.5,
so a memory found only by time scores $0.5/61$ at best. That ranks it
after every dense seed while the dense list has at most 62 entries
($1/(60 + r) > 0.5/61$ for $r \le 62$). The dense seed cap can reach 96 at
low Focus, and the late-interaction rerank after fusion can still promote
such a memory. With `as_of`, the cutoff $\tau_x \le T_q + 1$ also applies
to attached later turns and restatements. Unset, retrieval is byte-identical to the engine without the
channel (LoCoMo clock replay, 497 queries).

An oracle probe set $T_q$ to each LoCoMo question's earliest gold turn. Packet
evidence hits rose from 1,767 to 1,783 of 1,979 questions (17 gained, 1 lost),
and to 0.906 at weight 1.0. Query p50 rose by 0.07 to 0.17 ms (PR #31). This
bounds the mechanism; it is not a benchmark score.

Earlier builds also added an event-time recency tie-break to the dense score.
The round-3 ablation left every packet byte-identical without it, so it was
removed (@sec-math).

## Reciprocal-Rank Fusion

When any of the lexical, cross-modal or temporal channels returns hits, the
pool is ordered by reciprocal-rank fusion [@cormack2009reciprocal]:

$$
\mathrm{RRF}(m) = \sum_{\ell} w_\ell \,/\, \big(k + r_\ell(m)\big), \qquad k = 60,
$$

where $r_\ell(m)$ is $m$'s 1-based rank in list $\ell$. The dense seed list
(after member re-sorting) counts once with $w = 1$. The keyword list and each
per-modality cross-modal list count with $w = 1$, and the temporal list with
$w = 0.5$. Ties fall back to the semantic score and then to memory id. Only
the order changes; every candidate keeps its semantic score. $k = 60$ is the
constant of @cormack2009reciprocal; experiment-hook builds can override it,
release builds cannot. Without any auxiliary hits, the pool stays in dense
order.

## Neighbour Deferral

Hydration attaches each anchor's adjacent turns (@sec-hydration). A candidate
that is such a neighbour of a higher-ranked pick would spend an anchor slot on
content the packet already carries. Examples are a reply next to its
question, or the other half of an exchange. Within the output size, such
candidates are moved behind the picks, in order, so a short list still fills.
This costs one primary-key range lookup per pick.

## Late-Interaction MaxSim Rerank

After deferral, the head of the pool is reranked by a learned late-interaction
model [@khattab2020colbert] over the frozen AIST encoder
(`AIST-87M-LI.gguf`, `src/models/aist_late_interaction.cpp`). The constants
below are read from the shipped model file.

**Representation.** Every item becomes a set of unit vectors in one
$D = 64$-dimensional space. Items here are queries and stored members, in any
modality. The set has two sources.

* *Position features* through a per-tower linear map: text token hidden states
  (384-d, at most 256 positions) and image patch features (12 × 12 × 960-d).
  Audio has no trained map yet.
* The item's 256-d shared-space vector through one map shared by every
  modality.

**Memory side.** A stored payload's raw encoder positions (384-d text,
960-d image) are clustered into $K = 16$ spherical k-means centroids (8
Lloyd iterations, deterministic linspace initialization). Only then are the
centroids mapped into the 64-d space, normalized and quantized to int8. A
payload with 16 or fewer positions keeps all of its rows, so a blob holds up
to 16 codes: at most 1,028 bytes, a 4-byte header plus $16 \times 64$
codes. Codes are per member, computed at write time; there
is no shared codebook. Its stored global vector is mapped and int8-rounded at
query time the same way.

**Query side.** The query keeps every mapped position, plus its mapped global
vector. Text queries are capped at 128 positions; image queries keep all 144
patches. Each vector $q_r$ gets a softmax gate weight $w_r$ from
a learned linear gate.

**Scoring.** For member $s$ with vector set $V_s = Z_s \cup \{g_s\}$,

$$
\sigma(s) = \sum_r w_r \max_{v \in V_s} \langle q_r, v \rangle .
$$

Memory $m$ at first-stage pool position $\rho_m$ (0-based) scores a soft
maximum over its first 8 members plus a rank prior:

$$
\mathrm{LI}(m) = \alpha \cdot \tau \log \sum_{s \in m}
               e^{\sigma(s)/\tau}
             + \beta \cdot \log(1 + \rho_m) / \log 101.
$$

The shipped constants are $\alpha = 20.46$, $\tau = e^{-3.456} \approx
0.032$ and $\beta = -0.308$. The rank prior is how the rerank blends with the
first stage. At position 63 it subtracts 0.28, which is worth about 0.014 of
MaxSim similarity after the $\alpha$ scale: a small learned preference for
the fused order, not a veto.

**Depth and slots.** The rerank covers the top 64 candidates. Depth 64 keeps
its cost at 0.4 to 3 ms per query. A memory none of whose members has codes
keeps its slot, and the coded memories reorder among the remaining slots.
Uncoded memories come from towers without a trained map (audio) and from
signals stored before migration 54. One global vector cannot compete with a
code set, so moving these memories would bias against their modality. A query
without position vectors keeps the engine order.

The rerank runs after neighbour deferral on purpose. Deferring the
neighbours of the reranked picks instead lowered Eval 1 packet recall from
0.938 to 0.892.

**Training.** The model has 102,469 float32 weights (410 KB). It is
distilled from the `ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` cross-encoder with listwise KL at
temperature 2, plus a multi-positive listwise loss on gold memories. Image
members get soft labels through their BLIP captions and hard labels through
MemLens gold. Training pools come from LongMemEval-S, the LongMemEval
conversations of Eval 1, DolphinBench, MemLens and the BEAM 1M train
conversations. Held-out splits are 30% of Eval 1 and BEAM 1M conversations,
one DolphinBench persona, 20% of LongMemEval and MemLens questions, and the
whole 108-question MemLens image evaluation set. LoCoMo is never trained on.
@sec-experimental separates trained-on and zero-shot benchmarks accordingly.

**Effect.** Packet gold-turn recall rose on every set (PR #28, @sec-implementation):

* Eval 1: 0.846 to 0.938, and 0.878 to 0.955 on its conversations held out
  from training.
* LongMemEval-S: 0.808 to 0.992 (14 unseen questions 0.857 to 1.000).
* LongMemEval-M: 0.770 to 0.894.
* MemLens: text gold 0.415 to 0.575, image gold 0.344 to 0.396.
* BEAM at a 34,800-byte budget: 0.615 / 0.413 / 0.274 to 0.696 / 0.518 /
  0.369 at 100K / 1M / 10M. 100K and 10M were never trained on.

End-to-end BEAM scores (gpt-6.1-sol low answer and judge) rose from
0.816 / 0.778 / 0.667 to 0.843 / 0.799 / 0.699 (+0.027 [+0.006, +0.049],
+0.021 [+0.005, +0.036], +0.033 [+0.003, +0.063]). Query p95 stayed within
×1.00 to ×1.14 of the engine without the rerank, from 10k to 443k memories.
The codes added 11% to Eval 1 store size.

## Standing Memories

Some statements must shape answers long after they leave query similarity:
"Always include version numbers when I ask about libraries", "From now on,
answer in French". The engine keeps them in a small set ranked on its own.

* **Membership.** Membership belongs to the stored signal, not its memory
  (`standing_signals`, migration 53, replacing the memory-level set of
  migration 51). Under Natural retention a directive is one turn of a grouped
  memory several kilobytes long, which a memory-level check never admits.
* **Detector.** A pattern check over the signal's text, at most 480 bytes:
  a clause opening with *always*, *never*, *from now on*, *going forward*,
  *whenever I*, *I prefer* and similar, optionally after *please*. This is
  today's only detector.
* **Capacity.** The set keeps the newest 256 members.
* **Query.** Every query ranks the members written before $\tau_x$ by RRF
  ($k = 60$) of two lists. One is the cosine of $e_q$ to the member's own
  stored vector. The other is BM25 ($k_1 = 1.2$, $b = 0.75$) over the member's
  6-byte word stems, with document frequencies from the set itself.
  Store-wide frequencies would discount the topic words that tell directives
  apart.
* **Block.** The best 5, within 2 KiB, form a standing block
  (`Context::standing_memory`) ahead of the retrieved memories. Each entry
  holds only the directive signals of one memory.

The block takes no retrieved slot. A consumer that cuts the retrieved list at
$k$ keeps the same $k$ retrieved memories. When standing items took ranked
slots instead, LongMemEval-M gold recall at $k = 11$ fell by 0.087.

On BEAM, PR #28 reports the share of instruction-following gold turns (the
instruction and its acknowledgement) for the standing block (b5447e25)
against the engine without it. The share rose from 0.44 / 0.26 / 0.00 to
0.86 / 0.81 / 0.44 at 100K / 1M / 10M. @sec-implementation reports, for the
same channel, an overall gold-turn share gain of 0.070 / 0.075 / 0.053, no
other category losing more than 0.01, and query p95 within 0.98 / 0.96 /
1.14 of the engine without it.

## Ranking Invariants

* `source_id` and modality are never ranking inputs. Modality selects only
  which tower map and which cross-modal populations apply.
* Only the open write unit, and with `as_of` everything that starts after
  $T_q$, is excluded. `as_of` does not filter working memory, or the content
  of a retrieved memory that spans $T_q$ (PR #31).
* Every auxiliary channel adds candidates and rank mass and removes none.
* Every stage ends in a deterministic tie order (score, then memory id).
